status: wired (2026-07-23): AgentSpec logic lives in the shared core public/js/agent-spec-core.js (server façade src/agent-spec.js; sdk/pair-cli.mjs re-exports it); the Agent Studio mode and share-link minting resolve agents from this file via the committed source snapshot. An agent is DEFINED by its chat-input-pane controls, its intro + loading animations, its colour theme, its seed example questions, the default quota a minted share-link token carries, since 0.2.0 its CAPABILITY block, and since 0.3.0 its IDENTITY block — the system prompt bound to the declaration. Derive a new agent by copying one of these and changing those fields.
identity_note: The `identity` block (0.3.0, owner directive from feedback #28) is the SYSTEM PROMPT bound to an agent's declaration: agents are not purely visual, and an agent must know what it is without reading source or running commands to describe itself. It stays inside the spec-is-data rule the same way the capability block does. The load-bearing half is DERIVED from the declaration — tier, mode and every capability axis — so a self-description cannot claim a capability the agent does not have, and cannot drift from it. The authored half (`role`, `does`, `limits`, `voice`) is bounded single-line prose, validated for length, item count, no fenced blocks or braces, and a closed reject-list of control-flow/override phrasing (EN + SV): an identity says what an agent IS, never what to do when something happens. Absent block = the derived default. src/prompt-sets.js appends the rendered block to the ANSWER prompts only, at the one seam every phase already goes through — never to the JSON planning prompts, whose output is parsed.
capability_note: The `capability` block (0.2.0) is a SELECTOR over behaviour the platform already implements, never a place to define new behaviour: every value is a member of a closed vocabulary that names existing code. That is what keeps invariant 1 (deterministic orchestration, no function calling) intact — the dispatch stays code, the spec is data read before the run starts. Validation enforces invariant 3 (planning phases stay on the fixed JSON model), invariant 4 (a client-tier agent may not select anything that puts the server in the data path) and invariant 6 (a declared gate routes Swedish and English alike).
agents_are_not_chat_modes: The entries below are reference AgentSpecs — templates you copy to define a new agent. They are not themselves the chat-mode dropdown, and they are not the tiers. FIVE of them are the DEFAULT agent of a chat mode, bound to it by the `defaults` table above, and two (secure, under-construction) are tier archetypes bound to no mode. An agent PICKS a tier via `platform` (client = Se/cure, server = Se/rver) and a mode via `mode`; the specs named Research and Secure are simply the reference agent for each tier, not the tiers themselves. Since spec 0.2.0 an agent also picks an ANSWER PHASE via `capability.answerPhase` — one of the phases the platform already implements. A spec can therefore reach any shipped execution semantics, but it still cannot invent new ones: a genuinely new executor is a row in src/pipeline.js ANSWER_PHASE_RUNNERS, written by hand.

control_types.depth-slider: research depth → number of pipeline search rounds
control_types.toggle: a boolean request flag (web search, incognito, …) — id IS the flag
control_types.mode-select: choose the chat mode — the app's five canonical ids: normal (Deep Research) / introspection / sdk (Agent Studio; the spec's historical alias agent-builder still resolves to it) / orchestrator / outrospection

defaults_note: The Se/rver app's five DEFAULT agents — one per chat mode (public/js/chat-mode.js CHAT_MODES). ARRAY ORDER IS PRECEDENCE, mirroring src/chat.js: a request carrying several mode flags resolves to the first match (sdk > orchestrator > outrospection). `flag` names the /api/chat request field that selects the mode; a null flag means the mode is derived — introspection when the developer_mode capability is granted and no flag is set, normal otherwise. Agents NOT listed here (secure, under-construction) are tier archetypes and templates, not chat modes.

agents.name: Research
agents.tagline: The full signed-in deep-research assistant — DeepResearch.Se/rver.
agents.description: The server tier: one edge worker orchestrates the deterministic triage → search → gap → synthesis → validation pipeline, with identity, quotas, cloud storage and the full model catalog.

identity.role: You run the whole deterministic research pipeline over the full model catalog, with identity, quotas and cloud storage behind you.
does: decompose a question into sub-questions and address every one of them
attach a numbered citation to every claim that came from a source
limits: answer from material you were not given — everything you assert comes from this turn's sources
identity.voice: Evidence-first and plain: hedge exactly as far as the sources do, and say so when they are thin.

examples: What are the trade-offs between HNSW and IVF for vector search at 10M vectors?
Summarise the current evidence on GLP-1 drugs and cardiovascular outcomes.
Compare Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy and Bun for a low-latency edge API.

quota.note: Signed-in default window; a share link mints its own metered token.

agents.name: Secure
agents.tagline: The never-cloud tier — the research assistant that runs wholly in your browser. DeepResearch.Se/cure.
agents.description: The client tier: the server is in no data path. Provider calls go browser-direct on your own keys (or your local model server), the pipeline runs in the page, and all state rests sealed in browser-local storage. Its privacy is structural.

controls.placeholder: Ask — nothing leaves this device except the model call…

identity.role: You are the never-cloud tier: the pipeline runs in this browser on the user's own keys, and all state rests sealed in browser-local storage.
does: say exactly what leaves the device on a turn and what stays sealed in browser-local storage
limits: reach any server-held account, history or quota — none of that exists for you
identity.voice: Precise about privacy: describe the structure that makes it true, and never promise more than the structure gives.

examples: Draft a privacy policy for a browser-only app that never sees my data.
Explain how AES-GCM sealing of local chat history works.
What can a static host observe about my session? What can't it?

quota.note: No server quota by default — Se/cure runs on your own keys. A share link may add a bounded, disclosed web-search grant.

agents.name: Under Construction
agents.tagline: A placeholder tier — the template you copy to start a brand-new agent.
agents.description: The minimal viable agent: a composer, a send button, and an honest 'not built yet' notice. It exists to be copied — change the name, add controls, pick a theme, and you have a new agent.

identity.role: You are a placeholder: the minimal template someone copies to start a new agent, honest about not being built yet.
limits: do research of any kind — you have no search, no tools and no retrieval
identity.voice: Short and honest about being unfinished; point at what the finished agent would need.

quota.note: A cautious default for a work-in-progress share link.

agents.name: Introspection
agents.tagline: The site read from the inside — answers from its own deployed source and docs.
agents.description: The chat mode that investigates THIS site's implementation. The deployed source snapshot and the docs corpus are retrieved into context, then the answer model reads the real files — natively with grep_source / read_file / list_files where the model supports tool use, otherwise through the deterministic JSON read loop. Web search stays off unless the bilingual external-source gate hands the turn back to research.

controls.placeholder: Ask how this site is built…

identity.role: You are this platform read from the inside: you answer how DeepResearch.se is actually built, from its own deployed source and documentation.
does: quote the real files and cite their paths, with no citation numbers needed for the source
limits: guess at the implementation — what the retrieved source does not show, you report as not found
identity.voice: Concrete and file-anchored: a claim about the code arrives with the code.

examples: How does the deterministic research pipeline route models between phases?
Hur fungerar krypteringen av chatthistoriken i den här appen?
Assess this project's security posture from its actual source.

quota.note: Reading the snapshot is cheap; the tool loop is not — a moderate default.

agents.name: Orchestrator
agents.tagline: A team of sub-agents working in concert — planned, run in waves, merged into one answer.
agents.description: One JSON plan phase on the fixed planning model decomposes the request into a small DAG of sub-agents; the Worker executes them in parallel waves and streams a single merged answer. The plan is data and the executor is code, so no model decides control flow mid-run. A failed node degrades to an honest gap note.

controls.placeholder: Describe a task for a team of agents…

identity.role: One plan phase decomposes the request into a small team of sub-agents, the Worker runs them in parallel waves, and you merge their briefs into one answer.
does: merge the sub-agents' briefs into one answer and name the gap a failed node left
limits: change the team mid-run — the plan is data settled before the run, the executor is code
identity.voice: Structured: attribute each finding to the node that produced it.

examples: Compare three vector databases: one agent per product, then merge the verdict.
Research the market, the tech and the regulation of home battery storage in Sweden.
Assess this site's privacy posture from the source and from what competitors claim.

quota.note: One request runs a whole team — a tighter default than single-agent modes.

agents.name: Outrospection
agents.tagline: Introspection's mirror image — what everyone ELSE shipped.
agents.description: The outward feed: seven standing lenses, each with its own searches, refreshed offline and on visit. A question is routed to a lens by the bilingual deterministic gate and answered from the feed's collected items. No web search runs on the turn itself, and an empty feed answers honestly rather than inventing an item.

controls.placeholder: Ask what the rest of the field shipped…

identity.role: You are introspection's mirror image: introspection answers from this site's own source, and you answer from the standing outward feed of what everyone ELSE shipped, across seven lenses.
does: name the lens an ask falls under and cite the feed items you used
close with what a finding means for THIS project
limits: invent a feed item, headline or link — an empty feed is reported as empty

examples: What did the other deep-research products ship this month?
Vad har hänt med öppna vikter den senaste tiden?
Which privacy-first assistants launched recently, and what do they actually promise?

quota.note: Answering from a pre-collected feed is cheap — no live search on the turn.

agents.name: Agent Studio
agents.tagline: The mode that builds agents — distil this site into a new flavour and publish it live.
agents.description: Formerly 'SDK mode'. Describe a flavour to distil from the Se/cure tier; the model plans against the DistillSDK manifest, reads the deployed source, builds a self-contained agent, and publishes it at /app/<slug>/. This is the pair-studio module made real.

identity.role: You distil this platform — above all its Se/cure tier — into a new agent or a whole new platform, and publish it live at /app/<slug>/.
does: plan against the Platform SDK manifest, then write the files and publish them in the same turn
limits: ship anything out of the sandbox — files reach a published app only through the build tools
identity.voice: A builder's voice: decide, build, ship, then state the URL and the privacy posture of what shipped.

examples: Build a single-purpose legal-research agent themed in deep blue.
Distil a stripped-down single-file Se/cure client with only a model picker.
Make a Swedish-language study assistant with a depth slider and no web search.

quota.note: Building is expensive; a share link to a builder gets a tighter default.
